change_interpretations.engineering_summary: The allowed driver torque response time is reduced from 100 ms to 80 ms, requiring verification that the controller issues positive torque within 80 ms after a validated pedal input above 70 %.
A new timing constraint requires the emergency brake command to be issued within 80 ms of the brake input, adding a latency limit to the existing priority rule.

assessments.reason: The test measures driver torque response latency (procedure expects ≤100 ms) and recorded 94 ms PASS; the requirement VCU-DR-01 was tightened to 80 ms, so the previous evidence no longer meets the limit.
evidence: Procedure expects response ≤100 ms; previous result 94 ms PASS.
Requirement VCU-DR-01 changed from 100 ms to 80 ms.
Previous latency 94 ms exceeds new 80 ms limit.
assessments.recommended_action: Schedule a rerun of TV-001 with the acceptance criterion updated to ≤80 ms.

assessments.reason: The test checks arbitration between high pedal demand and emergency brake but does not record any timing, while both changed requirements now include latency limits.
evidence: Procedure applies 85 % pedal and emergency‑brake input; previous result PASS; no latency measured.
VCU-DR-01 now requires ≤80 ms torque response and VCU-BRK-03 adds ≤80 ms brake‑command latency.
assessments.recommended_action: Have the test owner decide whether TV-002 should be extended to capture the required response‑time measurements.

assessments.reason: The test records a maximum latency of 92 ms during a demand sweep, which would violate the new 80 ms limit, but it has no explicit link to VCU-DR-01.
evidence: Result 92 ms (PASS) under demand sweep.
Requirement VCU-DR-01 tightened to 80 ms.
No requirement link is present in the register entry.
assessments.recommended_action: Clarify whether TV-003 should be linked to VCU-DR-01 and, if so, plan a rerun to verify ≤80 ms.

assessments.reason: The test measures emergency‑brake command latency (88 ms PASS) against a 100 ms threshold, but VCU‑BRK‑03 now adds an 80 ms limit, so the previous evidence fails the new requirement.
evidence: Procedure targets brake command latency ≤100 ms; previous result 88 ms PASS.
Requirement VCU-BRK-03 now includes ≤80 ms brake‑command issuance.
Workshop note warns that brake‑latency measurements use a different clock and must be aligned.
assessments.recommended_action: Repeat TV-004 using the validated timing source and change the acceptance criterion to ≤80 ms.

assessments.reason: The test validates wheel‑speed sensor failure and degraded mode per VCU‑DGN‑04, which is unchanged and unrelated to the new timing constraints.
evidence: Requirement reference VCU-DGN-04 unchanged.
Test procedure checks sensor unplug and fault log; no timing involved.

assessments.reason: The test audits mode‑change logging per VCU‑LOG‑05; the changed requirements concern torque response and brake timing, not logging.
evidence: Requirement reference VCU-LOG-05 unchanged.
Procedure logs timestamp and build identifier; no latency measured.

assessments.reason: The test has a TBD requirement link and has not been run, making it impossible to determine relevance to the new timing changes.
evidence: Requirement_reference_raw is TBD; no linked requirement.
Previous result NOT RUN; no measured values.
assessments.recommended_action: Determine the correct requirement for TV-007 and decide if it needs to be updated for the new timing limits.

assessments.reason: The test replays an old diagnostic trace linked to an unknown legacy requirement and does not involve any of the changed timing requirements.
evidence: Requirement link VCU-OLD-88 is unknown; test checks non‑blocking status only.

assessments.reason: The test compares torque ramp profiles between Sport and Comfort modes per VCU‑MOD‑06, which does not include any latency or timing constraints.
evidence: Requirement reference VCU-MOD-06 unchanged; procedure has no quantitative response‑time assertion.

assessments.reason: The test verifies that a 7 ms pedal spike is filtered per VCU‑DR‑02; the changed requirements address response latency, not spike filtering.
evidence: Requirement VCU-DR-02 unchanged; procedure injects 7 ms pulse and checks no torque request.

assessments.reason: The test confirms brake‑priority torque cancellation but does not measure the 80 ms brake‑command issuance latency introduced by VCU‑BRK‑03.
evidence: Procedure verifies torque drop on emergency brake; no timing captured.
VCU-BRK-03 now adds ≤80 ms brake‑command latency.
assessments.recommended_action: Decide whether TV-011 should be extended to capture brake‑command latency and update the test accordingly.

assessments.reason: The wake‑up timing test concerns ECU power‑up readiness (500 ms) and is unrelated to the driver torque or brake timing changes.
evidence: Procedure verifies readiness within 500 ms; no link to VCU-DR-01 or VCU-BRK-03.
